exact_title: Read one discussion and preserve reply context when focusing unread entries
exact_body:
## Read a discussion with its reply context — estate-c6cc965b64c2 / native_engine

Under Jacob's current autonomous estate mandate, coordinated with the source integration lead.

### Observed student workflow
Current main `79a2f2b2cbb7e74128d731cf096c7e86f1942d4b`, tree `0114a6230c473c1ee1d01b99c7121c754b781d54`, can list discussion topics from the terminal. The existing Python `get_discussion()` and MCP tool already retrieve a topic and its cached reply view. The terminal has no command to open that topic, and neither surface offers an unread-focused view that keeps the parent entries needed to understand a reply.

A native Python 3.12.14 beforeimage preserves that distinction: the existing raw API returns the synthetic topic and three-entry tree through exactly two GETs, while `canvaspilot discussion 42 71` exits 2 with an unknown-command diagnostic. No source defect is asserted for the working raw API.

### Bounded additive scope
Add a pure `discussion_thread.py` report builder; a small `CanvasAPI.discussion_thread()` method that calls the unchanged raw reader; `discussion COURSE TOPIC [--unread-only]`; a matching curated MCP tool/catalog entry; focused authored tests and documentation.

The reader will retain original entry fields, stable positions within the returned reply tree, original parent IDs, participant attribution only when unambiguous, and reported read/forced-unread metadata. Focusing unread entries keeps their ancestors explicitly labeled as context. Missing or ambiguous facts remain unknown; malformed/unavailable responses remain visible errors.

The official [Discussion Topics API](https://developerdocs.instructure.com/services/canvas/resources/discussion_topics#method.discussion_topics_api.view) describes this view as cached and eventually consistent. The reader will identify that boundary. It will not label this as a fresh complete snapshot or quietly merge a separate entry stream.

### Ownership and qualification
Fresh project issue/PR and central HAMON #140 reads found no discussion-reader claimant. Grades #47/#50, self-submission attempts #48, assignment-list facts PR51, and inbox #49 remain with their owners. Existing `get_discussion`, topic listing, posting, transport/authentication/session broker, calendar and other curated methods remain unchanged.

Use the already available project Python runtime and synthetic fixture/loopback boundaries. Preserve exact source pins, original absent-command receipt, real CLI/MCP behavior, malformed/unknown and unread-ancestry controls, and unchanged owner test results where their dependencies are available. No dependency installation, native build, live school/account/browser operation, post, mark-read, subscription, group expansion or deployment is part of this scope.

Baseline driver SHA-256: `5950bcf18f1d6643015b9383f3684507e698c0bf529cd3039787320488253e82`. Initial custody: `/dev/shm/c6cc965b64c2-canvas-discussion`; source/evidence will be frozen for independent receiving before any source publication. The first attempt to write the receiver met shared ENOSPC before execution; that setup failure remains distinct from product evidence.
